gaps.why_now: A dedicated Phase 11 build entry now keeps the landed gpio_wdt starter and the survey checkpoint reviewable together instead of letting the lane drift after the first driver scaffold landed.
The survey gate now acts as a freshness check around the landed gpio_wdt starter so the lane does not drift back to pre-driver assumptions or overclaim broader watchdog progress.

The survey note now records the landed gpio_wdt starter together with the bounded validation matrix, descriptor preflight checkpoint, timeout-property checkpoint, drvdata ownership checkpoint, the first teardown-facing parity note, and the still-open failure-mode parity gap so the next Phase 11 step stays explicit without overstating broader watchdog progress.

The first gpio_wdt starter is now landed and models hw_algo parsing, heartbeat margin validation, bounded start or stop or ping transitions, a tiny probe-time summary, a nowayout-aware stop helper, and a registration-facing handoff summary without touching live GPIO or platform registration.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep the toggle and level state transitions, heartbeat validation, always-running stop behavior, nowayout-aware stop outcomes, descriptor preflight ordering, timeout-property ordering, drvdata ownership ordering, and registration handoff bookkeeping honest around the landed simple-driver scaffold.

A bounded slice note records exactly what the gpio_wdt starter, probe-summary helper, descriptor preflight helper, timeout-property helper, drvdata ownership helper, stop-policy helper, and registration handoff summary cover so later Phase 11 work can extend the model without reopening the starter contract.

A tiny teardown note now records the bounded meaning of the stop-policy split, the drvdata ownership checkpoint, and the registration handoff so the lane can name teardown-facing ownership without overclaiming live reboot or remove execution.

The bounded validation matrix now records the shared Phase 11 replay path, the current property, startup, descriptor-preflight, timeout-property, drvdata-ownership, runtime, teardown-note, and handoff evidence, and the explicit out-of-scope kernel-facing work so the review packet keeps one truthful validation posture.

The lane now lands a tiny probe-time summary for always-running startup, requested GPIO line mode, and watchdog-core-facing bookkeeping so the starter describes more of gpio_wdt_probe() before any live GPIO or platform glue.
The starter now lands a tiny nowayout-aware stop helper so review can distinguish watchdog-core stop blocking from hardware always-running behavior before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now adds a tiny registration-facing handoff summary so review can see whether startup state, stop policy, timeout init, and reboot bookkeeping reach watchdog-core registration before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now adds a tiny descriptor preflight summary so review can see the exact devm_gpiod_get() flag choice and the fact that descriptor lookup still sits before timeout parsing, always-running bookkeeping, and the registration-facing handoff without claiming live GPIO acquisition.

The starter now records one tiny timeout-property checkpoint so review can see that `hw_margin_ms` stays required, that descriptor lookup still precedes timeout parsing, and that timeout parsing still happens before always-running bookkeeping and the registration-facing handoff without claiming a live property or GPIO path.

The starter now records one tiny drvdata ownership checkpoint so review can see that parent linkage and module ownership stay attached, that timeout parsing still precedes the bounded drvdata bind, and that the same owner still reaches the registration-facing handoff without claiming live platform registration.

Platform-driver registration, GPIO descriptor acquisition, watchdog core registration, and reboot integration remain blocked until the lane grows one failure-mode or hardware-validation checkpoint beyond the descriptor preflight, timeout-property, drvdata ownership, teardown-note, and registration-handoff packet.
